1. Introduction

This manual documents operational procedures for the Atlas platform. It covers configuration, monitoring, troubleshooting, and safety protocols. Read this document before performing any maintenance tasks.

All personnel must follow the steps in the order presented. Deviations require written approval from the operations lead. Keep this document accessible at all times.

2. Safety Protocols

Safety is the highest priority. Always wear required personal protective equipment when entering data centers. Follow lockout-tagout procedures before touching hardware.

Report incidents immediately using the incident form. Do not attempt repairs beyond your certification level. Emergency contacts are posted near each equipment rack.

3. Access Control

Access to Atlas resources is governed by role-based policies. Request access through the identity portal. Approval chains vary by sensitivity level.

Review permissions quarterly. Remove access promptly when roles change. Audit logs are retained for 24 months and reviewed monthly.

4. Configuration Management

All configuration changes must be recorded in the change management system. Use version control for configuration files. Test changes in staging before production rollout.

Rollback plans are required for every change. Document dependencies and expected impact. Communicate maintenance windows to stakeholders at least 48 hours in advance.

5. Incident Response

Incidents are classified by severity. Use the incident command system to coordinate response. Document actions in real time. Communicate status updates every 15 minutes for P1 incidents.

Conduct post-incident reviews within 48 hours. Identify root cause and preventive actions. Update runbooks based on lessons learned.

6. Monitoring

Monitoring covers infrastructure, application, and business metrics. Dashboards are organized by domain. Alerts are routed to on-call rotations via paging services.

Tune alert thresholds regularly to reduce noise. Use anomaly detection for unpredictable patterns. Document dashboard ownership and refresh cadence.

7. Backup and Recovery

Backups are taken daily and retained for 30 days. Test restores monthly to validate integrity. Store backups in geographically separate regions.

Document recovery time objectives and recovery point objectives. Update procedures after schema changes. Encrypt backups at rest and in transit.

8. Networking

Network topology is documented in the architecture repository. Use private endpoints for internal traffic. Enable TLS on all public interfaces.

Monitor bandwidth utilization and latency between regions. Configure firewalls with deny-by-default rules. Review network access lists quarterly.

9. Security

Security controls include encryption, intrusion detection, and vulnerability scanning. Apply patches within 30 days of release. Conduct penetration tests annually.

Review security policies after any incident. Maintain a inventory of sensitive data. Report suspicious activity to the security operations center.

10. Change Management

All changes must be recorded in the change management system. Emergency changes require post-approval within 24 hours. Standard changes follow a pre-approved workflow.

Coordinate changes across teams to avoid conflicts. Use change freezes for critical business periods. Review change success rates monthly.
